Rule: An agent principal cannot exist without a named accountable human owner.
A principal sees data only for the legal entities granted to it.
A principal sees time data only for the locations granted to it.
Effective scope is the intersection of tenant, entity, location, reporting line and payroll group.
Compensation fields return null to a principal outside the record's payroll group, even where time fields are visible.
Every approvable request routes through one chain definition resolved by request type, worker class, location and amount band.
Each step resolves its approver by role, position or named person, and starts an SLA clock.
An approval queued against a principal who has left reroutes to the successor or the role holder; it never vanishes.
A decision records actor, timestamp, channel and, on rejection or return, a reason.
Steps are sequential and mandatory unless the definition marks a step optional.
HR may edit or close a request at any stage; the edit is logged with actor and reason.
A temporal fact is never updated in place; a new version is written and the prior version end-dated.
An as-at read takes valid_at and recorded_at; payroll and recompute must pass the snapshot timestamp, not now.
Search for an existing person before creating one.
Parameters: match keys: name, DOB, mobile, PAN, Aadhaar

Rule: A duplicate candidate above the confidence threshold is presented to HR for a decision, never auto-merged or auto-rejected.
A person record is created once and survives rehire, conversion and entity transfer.
An Aadhaar or PAN mismatch does not block joining; it raises a payroll-blocking flag.
Client value / default: Blocking at payroll, not at hire

Rule: An assignment can only be created against a vacant, non-frozen, non-abolished position.
An assignment belongs to an employment, which belongs to a legal entity.
Payroll group and location are independent attributes of an assignment; neither defaults from the other.
Worker class supplies policy defaults; the assignment may override any of them with a reason and an effective date.
Creating an assignment triggers the joining chain.
Any assignment change carries an effective date and a reason.
A retro change effective inside a closed payroll period produces arrears in the next open run; the closed run is never rewritten.
A change to class, rest days, shift group, grace exemption or location queues an attendance recompute for the affected range.
Worker class attributes are read as at the reference date, not as at today.
An assignment-level override without a reason fails validation at write time.
Grace exemption is an attribute of the designation band, never a hardcoded grade string.
Policy resolution for a date outside the assignment span returns 'not employed', not defaults.
Sanctioned strength is recorded by org unit, designation and location with an effective date and an approver.
Filled and open counts are derived from assignments and requisitions; neither is stored.
Headroom = sanctioned − filled − open requisitions.
On separation the position is marked vacant with last incumbent and vacated date.
Every uploaded document carries a class and, where applicable, an expiry date.
Extraction never overwrites a verified value; low confidence routes to a verification queue.
Document expiry generates reminders at configured intervals.
A punch is captured from any enrolled source and stored immutably.
Client value / default: Biometric, mobile, WhatsApp, kiosk, web, gate

Rule: Offline punches are queued locally with a signed timestamp and replayed on reconnect.
Device clock drift is corrected using the device's last sync offset; the raw value is retained alongside the correction.
Duplicate punches inside the dedupe window are marked, not discarded.
Every landed punch queues the affected attendance day for derivation.
A punch arriving for a locked payroll period raises an exception instead of changing the locked day.
An attendance day is keyed on the date the SHIFT started, not the calendar date of the punch.
Events inside the day window are ordered by timestamp before pairing.
IN pairs to the next OUT; an unpaired event raises an exception and is never discarded.
Every gap between consecutive segments is written as a break row with a type and a paid flag.
gross_minutes = last_out − first_in.
Whether recorded breaks are deducted from net is tenant configuration.
Approved personal gate-pass minutes are credited back into work hours before disposition thresholds are applied.
Overtime = max(0, basis_minutes − shift_minutes), where basis is gross or net per tenant configuration.
Every attendance day stores computed_at and the ruleset version that produced it.
Recomputation writes an audit delta; recomputing an unchanged day produces an identical row and no delta.

Rule ID: § TIME — SHIFT, DAY TYPE AND DISPOSITION

Rule: The assigned shift comes from the published roster, falling back to the assignment default.
Inference windows must not overlap within a shift group; overlapping configuration fails validation at save.
Where the in-punch falls in another shift's window inside the group, that shift is adopted, with assigned and inferred both recorded.
An HR override of an inferred shift is logged with actor and reason.
Threshold lookup uses the APPLIED shift's duration, not the assigned shift's.
Day type is resolved from the location's work and holiday calendar.
The worker class's rest-day policy overlays the calendar.
Policy attaches to worker class, never to the contractor engagement.
Client value / default: Class is the unit of policy

Rule: Day type is written before thresholds are applied.
On a non-working day type, thresholds are skipped and status reflects the day type.
Disposition thresholds are looked up by shift duration from a configuration table.
Below the absent threshold the day is Absent.
Below the half-day threshold the day is Half Day.
Grace applies to both the in and the out punch.
Grace-exempt bands incur no late instance and no deduction.
Late instances are counted per calendar month and the count is visible to the employee.
From the fourth late instance in a month, each late arrival beyond grace marks the day Half Day.
An employee who finished after the long-night hour may arrive within the relief window the next day and still be credited a full day.
The status stores the IDs of the rules that produced it.
A gate pass carries a type: personal or official.
Personal gate passes are capped per calendar month by total minutes and by instance count.
Approved personal gate-pass minutes are added to work hours; unapproved absence stays deducted.
Official gate passes are tracked but do not consume the personal ceiling.
Overtime payability is decided by the resolved ot_eligibility, not by hours alone.
Eligibility none means zero payable overtime; raw minutes are still retained for reporting.
For rest_day_and_holiday_only, weekday overtime is zero and rest-day or holiday working pays the whole span.
The overtime multiplier comes from the state rule pack; exceeding statutory weekly limits warns the approver.
Overtime is tagged to the run that will pay it, which may be an off-cycle run.
Exceptions are raised for unpaired punches, missing days, device failure, inferred shifts and threshold crossings.
An agent may propose a regularisation but only auto-resolve under the tenant's configured threshold.
An approved regularisation queues recompute and closes the exception.
The recompute queue carries person, date range and reason.
Recompute reads every input as at the recompute snapshot, never as at today.
Recompute runs in an isolated worker and must not degrade interactive latency.
Recompute never alters a locked or closed payroll period; it raises an arrears item instead.
Deltas feed the pre-payroll audit check for days not recomputed since the last rule change.
Team history is scoped by the manager's reporting line, evaluated at query time.
Team history returns attendance, leave, overtime, gate pass, late status and applied shift per day.
Exports of personal data are logged.
Accrual is bound to the leave band through an accrual policy.
Standard-band employees accrue no earned leave for six months, then receive a single credit on completion.
Accrual and expiry jobs are idempotent per person, type, period and transaction type.
AGM and above receive 18 EL, 6 CL and 6 SL on 1 January; all others 1.5 EL per month plus 6 CL and 6 SL.
Casual and sick leave for a new joiner are prorated by joining month from a table.
Client value / default: Jan 6 · Feb-Mar 5 · Apr-May 4 · Jun-Jul 3 · Aug-Sep 2 · Oct-4 Dec 1

Rule: Prorated credits post to the ledger citing the proration rule as source.
Leave eligibility follows the worker class; ineligible classes accrue nothing.
A leave request captures type, dates, half-day flags and reason.
Balance is projected from the ledger as at the leave start date, honouring per-credit expiry.
Casual leave cannot be taken with, or merged into, earned or sick leave.
Monthly caps: two casual leave days and ten earned leave days per calendar month.
Validation runs before the approval chain starts and the message names the rule that blocked it.
Approval debits the ledger against the specific credits consumed, so a reversal knows where to return days.
Early return records the actual return date inside the approved span.
The reversal row and the attendance recompute happen in ONE transaction.
Days after the actual return become Present or their punch-derived status.
An early return affecting a locked period produces arrears, not a change to the closed run.
Each comp-off credit carries its own expiry clock from its own credit date.
Comp-off consumption draws from the earliest-expiring open credit first.
Unconsumed comp-off lapses by a Lapse row on its own expiry date.
A comp-off clock may cross the leave-year boundary; the year end does not truncate it.
At year end earned leave encashes above the carry-forward cap; casual and sick leave lapse.
Encashment is raised as a payroll input computed on the statutory wage base.
Birthday leave is a separate credit with its own eligibility window.
Balance = credits − debits − lapses − encashments + reversals, as at a date.
The balance screen exposes the transactions that produced it.
A payroll run carries a run type and a period may carry several runs.
The run population is resolved from assignments active in the period, including joiners, leavers and transfers.
Inputs are pulled from attendance, leave, gate pass, overtime, claims, arrears and payroll_input rows.
Locking inputs freezes the run against further input changes.
The snapshot hashes inputs, rule pack versions and configuration so the run can be recomputed and matched to the paisa.
Pre-payroll audit runs rule-based checks first and statistical checks second.
An agent may classify and draft resolutions but never change a payroll figure.
A CRITICAL flag blocks approval and cannot be waived below its configured role threshold.
Pay components form a DAG evaluated in topological order, once per employee.
Money is held as integers in the smallest currency unit; no floating point anywhere in the engine.
Proration across any month boundary sums to the full-month value.
Every payslip line stores the node, inputs, output and rule pack version that produced it.
Statutory wage base = basic + dearness allowance + retaining allowance.
Where excluded components exceed 50% of total remuneration, the excess is added back to the wage base.
The wage base is one node, computed once, and consumed by PF, ESI, gratuity, bonus, overtime and encashment.
A structure change can be simulated for statutory cost and take-home impact before adoption.
Daily-wage earnings are a separate DAG node selected by wage_type, not a proration parameter on the monthly node.
Daily-wage earnings = days present × daily rate, with half days at the configured fraction.
The day count is shown on the payslip so a daily-wage worker can reconcile against attendance.
PF and EPS are computed on the statutory wage base against the ceiling in the effective rule pack.
An employee crossing the ESI wage threshold mid-period continues contributing to the end of the contribution period.
Professional tax follows the location's state slab set; it does not apply in every state.
TDS respects the regime choice and projects to year end; a mid-year switch is an expected case.
Gratuity and bonus provisions accrue on the statutory wage base for the journal.
Payroll recovers loan instalments; it does not originate loans or judge eligibility.
A recovery that would drive net below the floor is reduced or skipped, flagged, and carried forward.
Recovery stops when outstanding reaches zero.
The closing outstanding is reported back to the loans module and to the GL.
Review shows variance against the prior period and a headcount reconciliation.
A run cannot reach APPROVED with an open CRITICAL flag or an unmapped pay component.
Bank file totals are verified out of band under dual control, and bank-detail changes inside a payroll window raise an alert.
After DISBURSEMENT_PREPARED, corrections happen only as arrears.
Each run emits its own journal.
An off-cycle overtime run is a second run against the same period, not a delayed line in the first.
An off-cycle run pulls only the overtime records tagged to it.
Overtime pay uses the statutory wage base and the state multiplier.
An off-cycle run produces its own payslip view, bank file and journal, with run type as a journal dimension.
A full-and-final run cannot proceed while any blocking clearance item is open or unwaived.
F&F computes salary to the last working day, encashment, gratuity, notice recovery and loan foreclosure; negative net is a valid outcome.
F&F settles on the last working day when clearance has run in parallel with notice.
Payslip retrieval takes a period AND a run selector.
Every payslip line drills to the rule and the inputs behind it.
A rule pack is versioned, effective-dated, jurisdiction-scoped and carries a changelog citing its source notification.
Every rule in a pack has golden cases verified by hand against the statute.
A single golden-case mismatch fails the build.
A pack cannot deploy without a green suite and a named reviewer.
State packs layer on the central pack in a defined order.
The obligation calendar is generated per entity and state from the applicability matrix.
Filing packs are assembled from posted records only, never from typed figures.
A human files; the system prepares, records the acknowledgement and closes the obligation.
The applicable statutory form set follows the plant's registration, not the company's.
Form generation binds a declarative query to a template so a state amendment is a configuration change.
Statutory joining forms including Form F are generated inside the joining chain.
A filed form retains its acknowledgement reference against the period.
A workflow instance pins its definition version; in-flight instances finish on the version they started under.
The joining chain creates or adopts the person and assignment.
Statutory registrations are steps in the joining chain with owners and SLAs.
A bank-detail capture or change inside a payroll window raises an alert.
Policy acknowledgements retain the policy version acknowledged.
Induction learning paths are assigned by the joining chain using the standard assignment mechanism.
Every asset allocation becomes a clearance item at exit.
Lifecycle events generate announcements subject to the audience rule and an editorial override.
The clearance checklist is instantiated from a template resolved by worker class and location.
Clearance items run in parallel with the notice period, each with its own SLA.
F&F is held while any blocking item is open.
A blocking item may be waived by an authorised role with a reason, and any value becomes a recovery line.
Pending approvals across every module appear in one queue.
Every notification is actionable in place, on any channel.
An item shows the rule context that affects the decision.
Assistant answers are scoped to the asking employee's own permissions.
No assistant answer is produced without a retrieved source.
Assistant writes require explicit confirmation; reads may be automatic.
When the assistant does not know, it creates a ticket and says so.
Loan eligibility is one service method consumed by the application screen, the guarantor lock, the payroll node and the agent tool.
A person with an outstanding loan is ineligible for another loan and for a salary advance until full repayment.
A person standing guarantor on an unreleased loan is ineligible for their own loan and to stand guarantor again.
The ceiling is four times monthly basic, rising to six times for service above five years.
Eligibility returns a decision, a ceiling and the reasons, and the reasons are shown to the applicant.
A loan application names its proposed guarantors.
Two guarantors are mandatory; a third is optional above a configured amount threshold.
Accepting a guarantee locks the guarantor until release.
A director may sanction on special terms, bypassing eligibility, recorded with approver, reason and the rules waived.
Sanction creates the loan, the schedule and the payroll deduction node.
Each recovery posts a repayment row and reduces outstanding.
Outstanding reaching zero closes the loan.
Closure writes explicit guarantor release rows; release is an event, not an inference.
A requisition declares itself a replacement or an addition.
A replacement names a vacated position code and consumes no fresh sanctioned strength.
An addition exceeding sanctioned strength for the org unit, designation and location is blocked at approval.
An authorised role may override a sanction block with a recorded reason.
A referral is a named source channel carrying an award.
Referral awards mature in parts: on joining and on confirmation.
Client value / default: Part on joining, balance on confirmation

Rule: Referral and recognition payouts run through payroll in a named run.
Contractor invoices are submitted against a deployed population by class and rate.
Invoices reconcile against attendance the system already holds, with variance visible before payment.
Variance evidence is attached to the invoice decision.
A recognition award carries a citation, a period and an optional monetary component.
A monetary award raises a payroll input in a named run, never a side payment.
Awards publish an announcement referencing the award.
Letters are produced from versioned templates with merge fields.
The system drafts and a human reviews; nothing is issued directly from a model.
An issued letter retains the template version that produced it.
Master-data direction is a per-tenant choice of Nucleus-owned, ERP-owned or co-owned.
In co-owned mode no field has two owners and every mandatory field has one.
Inbound sync runs through the integration service; domain modules never call the ERP directly.
Upserts are idempotent on the external employee code and rejected on a repeated payload hash.
A conflict on a Nucleus-owned field is held for review; conflict policy is explicit configuration, never implicit last-write-wins.
ERP-owned fields are read-only in the Nucleus UI.
An unmatched external employee code is parked for resolution and never auto-creates a person.
Cost is split at employee level from the assignment as it stood in the pay period, before aggregation.
Client value / default: Cost centre, department, location, project, custom

Rule: Every pay component in a run must have a GL mapping before the run can be approved.
One balanced journal per run per legal entity, with run type as a dimension.
Delivery is by API, structured file, staging table or manual download, and the result is recorded either way.
The finance system's document number is written back onto the payroll run.
Seven reconciliation assertions must pass and be shown passing: gross, net vs bank, statutory vs challan, dimension residue, overtime, loan movement, drill-through.
Every GL line drills back to contributing employees and payslip lines.
An agent is a first-class principal with its own ID, scoped role and accountable human owner.
Tools are the only interface; agents never touch the database, call internal functions or hold credentials.
Every agent action passes the policy gate: permission, tenant policy, value and blast-radius caps.
Any tool classified write or above produces a dry-run diff before execution.
Nothing irreversible executes without a named human: disbursement, termination, offer release, statutory filing, loan sanction.
Every action lands in the append-only ledger with plan, simulation, approval, outcome and a reversal handle.
